transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-12 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Thompson (ArborTech Head of Security), Diego Martinez (CTO), Priya Rao (Compliance), Ethan Cole (Platform)

[00:00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call please.
[00:00:10] Lena (ArborTech): Lena here.
[00:00:12] Diego (CTO): Diego, hi.
[00:00:14] Priya (Compliance): Priya.
[00:00:16] Ethan (Platform): Ethan.
[00:00:18] Maya (SE): Maya from Redwood.
[00:00:20] Jordan (AE): Great. Agenda today is security checkpoints during the pilot: SSO/SCIM, audit logs & retention, SOC 2 evidence, and any blockers for the POC tuning.

[00:00:45] Diego (CTO): Quick context: pilot traffic is synthetic plus a small subset of redacted records, we need assurances for short-term retention and ability to purge. Also want to validate SAML flows for SSO.

[00:01:05] Lena (Head of Security): On my side, main asks — we need audit logs with user identity mapping, admin actions traced, and immutable logs for at least 90 days during the pilot. Also want clarity on encryption at rest keys and if Redwood supports customer-managed KMS or HSM.

[00:01:40] Maya (SE): For the pilot we can enable enhanced audit logging. Logs include request id, route/model, token counts, caller identity (subject from SAML/SCIM), and action type. We can also stream logs to your syslog endpoint or S3, or provide a syslog/syslog-ng collector.

[00:02:10] Priya (Compliance): Are the logs tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody-ish properties for changes to admin roles.

[00:02:25] Maya (SE): They’re write-once to our internal logging pipeline for the hosted pilot; we can also forward signed logs to your SIEM. For production Dedicated/Private, you get full control over where logs live.

[00:02:50] Ethan (Platform): How about retention — can we set it to 30 days or 90? Pilot specifically wants 90 but we don't want long-term retention beyond agreed deletion.

[00:03:05] Jordan (AE): We can set pilot retention to a customer-configured window up to 90 days. After the pilot we can run a purge script and provide a deletion manifest.

[00:03:30] Diego (CTO): Good. On SSO: we use Azure AD, SCIM provisioner, and need group sync so roles are mapped. Is SCIM supported in the POC?

[00:03:50] Maya (SE): Yes, we support SCIM for user provisioning in hosted and private. For the hosted pilot, we can enable a scoped SCIM endpoint tied to your tenant. Mapping docs are in our security pack, but I'll share specific attributes we support.

[00:04:15] Priya (Compliance): We also need SAML metadata and an assertion example for our IdP. Plus, what about session lifetime and token refresh?

[00:04:30] Maya (SE): We'll share SAML metadata. Sessions are short-lived bearer tokens; refresh windows are configurable, default 1 hour. For the pilot we can reduce session length as an extra control.

[00:05:00] Lena (Head of Security): KMS — do you support customer-managed keys in the hosted offering or is that only in Private?

[00:05:10] Jordan (AE): Customer-managed KMS is available in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer provider-managed keys but can integrate with partner KMS in some enterprise deals. For the pilot we can provide encryption details and key handling practices.

[00:05:40] Lena: If KMS isn't available for hosted, we'd need strong compensating controls: strict RBAC, logged admin actions, and guaranteed deletion after the pilot.

[00:06:00] Maya: Agreed — we can enable admin RBAC, MFA for all console users, and provide an audit trail of admin changes. We'll also hand over a deletion manifest when the pilot ends.

[00:06:30] Diego: SOC 2 — do you have Type II? We need the report and any SOC 2 scope items, especially about availability and confidentiality controls.

[00:06:45] Jordan: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II. I'll share the report and a summary of scope controls (redacted as needed) after the call.

[00:07:05] Priya: Can you also include evidence around access reviews and change management? We need sample runbooks to show controls.

[00:07:20] Jordan: We'll include the relevant excerpts and a short runbook sample showing employee access review cadence.

[00:07:40] Ethan: For audit logs, what fields are available? We need user email, subject, action, request payload hash, model used, and timestamps.

[00:08:00] Maya: The current schema includes timestamp, request_id, caller_subject (email), route, model_name, tokens_in/out counts, http_status, and an event_type code. We can add payload hash as an optional field for the pilot.

[00:08:30] Lena: Will the logs include the prompt text? For our pilot we only want redacted content — we preferred only metadata and a hash instead of full text.

[00:08:45] Maya: We can redact prompt text and record a prompt_hash; full-text logging is off by default for the pilot. If you want to capture full-text for evaluation, we suggest using ephemeral tokenized captures and then deleting.

[00:09:10] Priya: Deletion guarantees — how do you prove deletion? We need an auditable deletion log and ideally a verification digest after purge.

[00:09:30] Maya: We’ll run the purge, produce a deletion manifest listing objects removed with checksums, and provide a signed confirmation from our systems team. For hosted pilots the manifest is sufficient; Dedicated/Private gives you direct access to storage.

[00:09:55] Diego: Networking — is a VPC peering option possible during pilot if we need to avoid public endpoints?

[00:10:10] Jordan: For short pilots we usually don't do VPC peering because of setup time, but we can offer a restricted IP allowlist and mutual TLS for ingestion endpoints. If you need VPC, we can scope it as a follow-up and estimate 2-3 weeks for setup.

[00:10:35] Ethan: We might need that depending on compliance signoff. Can you provide estimated timelines?

[00:10:45] Jordan: IP allowlist & SAML & logging changes — we can do within the week. VPC peering estimate is 2–3 weeks.

[00:11:05] Lena: On personnel access — who at Redwood will have visibility into our pilot data? We need a list of roles with access and justification.

[00:11:20] Maya: Access is limited to platform engineers by role, never beyond SOC 2 scoped admins. We'll provide a role map and an access justification log for the pilot.

[00:11:45] Priya: Great. Also want assurance about incident response and breach notifications — 72 hours SLA?

[00:12:00] Jordan: Our standard enterprise incident notification is 72 hours for confirmed incidents; we'll include the incident response contacts in the documents.

[00:12:20] Diego: Are there any live demo items we should run to validate these? For example, provision a test user via SCIM, trigger a signed log entry, and then run the purge.

[00:12:35] Maya: Yes — proposed demo flow: 1) Provision via SCIM, 2) Authenticate via SAML, 3) Execute a sample request (redacted), 4) Verify audit event forwarded to your SIEM, 5) Run purge and show deletion manifest. We can run that in a 30–45 minute SE-led session.

[00:13:05] Lena: That demo would answer most of our questions. Let's schedule it and include our SIEM admin.

[00:13:20] Jordan: I'll coordinate — target the week after next (2025-03-20) for the security deep dive.

[00:13:40] Ethan: A few nitty-gritty items: do you support SAML attribute mapping for groups-to-roles? And can SCIM do group sync?

[00:13:55] Maya: Yes to both. SCIM group sync supported; SCIM v2 patch/create semantics handled. We'll share attribute mapping examples.

[00:14:20] Priya: Regarding log storage, if logs are forwarded to our S3 bucket, are they encrypted at rest using our KMS?

[00:14:35] Maya: If we forward to your S3, you control the bucket and KMS keys. For hosted forwarding we can push encrypted objects to your bucket using your KMS policy.

[00:14:55] Diego: Excellent. On SOC 2 evidence — will you attach timestamps and reviewers for access reviews? We need to show periodic reviews in our compliance docs.

[00:15:10] Jordan: Yes — we'll include examples of access review logs with timestamps and reviewer IDs.

[00:15:30] Lena: Slight concern — some words were previously wrong in your automated docs, e.g., 'KV cache' spelled oddly in older reports. Not a big deal but consistency matters.

[00:15:45] Maya: Thanks for flagging — we'll audit doc nomenclature in shared artifacts.

[00:16:05] Diego: Anything on data residency? For the pilot, data will be processed in us-east-1, is that acceptable?

[00:16:15] Priya: Our policy prefers US/EU only; for now us-east-1 is fine but will need EU region for production.

[00:16:30] Jordan: Noted — we process pilot in us-east-1; production can be pinned to EU region.

[00:16:50] Ethan: Are there metrics or dashboards to show token usage per user so we can reconcile billing and security?

[00:17:05] Maya: Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns per API key and per route. We can generate CSV exports for your finance and security teams.

[00:17:30] Lena: Good. One more — background checks for engineers with access? Do you have attestations?

[00:17:45] Jordan: Employee background checks are part of our HR controls scoped in SOC 2. We'll include a redacted attestation in the pack.

[00:18:10] Priya: On logging, can you provide an example event for an admin role change? I want to see the fields.

[00:18:25] Maya: Example event schema will be in the doc I'll send — includes admin_id, action, target_user, timestamp, request_id, and before/after roles.

[00:18:45] Diego: For the demo, can we also see the signed log forwarding to Splunk? Our SIEM is Splunk Cloud.

[00:19:00] Maya: We support Splunk HTTP Event Collector ingestion; we'll add your SIEM admin to the invite.

[00:19:20] Jordan: Quick recap: Jordan sends SOC2 report + arch diagram; Maya shares SAML metadata and SCIM mapping; we'll schedule SE-led demo 2025-03-20; ArborTech validates log fields and retention; action owners and due dates noted.

[00:19:45] Priya: Sounds good. A small question on legal: if we escalate to procurement, do you have a standard pilot MSA or DPA?

[00:19:58] Jordan: Yes we have a POC-specific DPA and a one-page pilot addendum we can attach. I'll push those to Diego and Priya after the call.

[00:20:20] Diego: Great. Any blockers from Redwood to enable the above this week?

[00:20:32] Maya: No blockers — SCIM/SAML and logging toggles are quick. We'll just need a test user and your SAML metadata.

[00:20:50] Ethan: I'll provision a test account and share SAML metadata to maya@redwood.ai.

[00:21:05] Lena: Also please include a brief runbook for deletion and emergency contact list in the packet.

[00:21:20] Jordan: Will do. Anything else?

[00:21:30] Priya: One last item — can Redwood sign an NDA for any exchanged screenshots or logs we may share?

[00:21:40] Jordan: Yes, we can sign a mutual NDA. I'll coordinate with legal.

[00:22:00] Diego: Perfect. If we don't have other questions let's close and capture action items.

[00:22:10] Jordan: Closing notes: expect docs from me by Friday (2025-03-14). Next meeting: security deep dive/demo 2025-03-20, Jordan/Maya will lead.
[00:22:25] Lena: Thanks all.
[00:22:28] Maya: Thanks.
[00:22:30] (end of recording)

Notes: Shared artifacts referenced during the call — "SOC2 report (shared link)" https://redwood-demo.s3/arbortech/soc2-type2.pdf; "SCIM mapping doc" https://redwood-demo.s3/arbortech/scim-mapping.md; "Deletion manifest template" https://redwood-demo.s3/arbortech/deletion-manifest-template.csv

Quality notes: Transcription is machine-generated; occasional mis-hear (e.g., 'KMS' transcribed as 'kms', 'KV cache' variations).
